canonical_statement: The pilot study aimed to identify experiences related to misophonia symptoms and assess the feasibility and preliminary effectiveness of EMDR for reducing misophonia symptoms and improving general mental functioning and quality of life.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This pilot study aimed first to identify relevant experiences related to misophonia symptoms and secondly to reduce misophonia symptoms with EMDR therapy for reprocessing maladaptive implicit memories.

canonical_statement: Inclusion required a diagnosis of misophonia and age 18 to 65 years.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Inclusion criteria were diagnosis of misophonia (Schröder et al., 2013) and aged between 18 and 65 years.

canonical_statement: Exclusion criteria included previous EMDR for misophonia, specified primary psychiatric disorders, recent substance-related disorder, recent CNS disorder or stroke, current benzodiazepine or stimulant use, suicide risk, and language barriers or illiteracy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Exclusion criteria were: previous EMDR treatment for misophonia, the presence of depression and anxiety disorder as a primary diagnosis, bipolar disorder, autism spectrum disorders, schizophrenia or any other psychotic disorder, substance-related disorder during the past 6 months, any structural central nervous system disorder or stroke within the last year, currently taking benzodiazepines or stimulants, patients at risk for suicide and patients with language barriers or illiteracy.

exclusion_criteria: Depression or anxiety disorder as primary diagnosis

canonical_statement: Ten participants were included at baseline; nine were female, mean age was 35 years, and mean age at misophonia onset was 13.10 years.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A total of 10 patients (9 [90%] female; mean [SD] age, 35 [14,53] years) were included (Table 1). Mean (SD) age of onset was 13.10 (9.75).

population.label: Included adults with misophonia at baseline

canonical_statement: Emotionally disturbing misophonia-related memories were identified in eight of ten baseline participants; those eight received EMDR, seven completed treatment and post-treatment measures, and one dropped out after the first session.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In eight of the 10 patients, misophonia-related emotionally disturbing memories were identified; the other two patients were excluded from the study. Seven patients completed EMDR-therapy and the post-treatment measures. Only one patient dropped out after the first EMDR session.

population.label: Adults with misophonia who received EMDR because misophonia-related emotionally disturbing target memories were identified

canonical_statement: EMDR was delivered using the standard eight-phase protocol.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The EMDR therapy was conducted according to the standard eight-phase protocol by Shapiro using the Dutch translation of the EMDR protocol.

concept.text: Eye movement desensitization and reprocessing (EMDR) therapy

exposures.details: Standard eight-phase protocol; sessions lasted 60-90 minutes; targets were emotionally disturbing memories related to onset or worsening of misophonia.

canonical_statement: Target memories were identified with a standardized time-line strategy focused on when misophonia symptoms started and worsened; targets were processed in temporal order.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The memories EMDR focused on were identified (phase 1) following a standardized search strategy called time-line path in the first session ... The order of targets was set; starting with targets that were related to the onset of the misophonia symptoms and subsequently, the memories of the events after which symptoms worsened.

concept.text: Eye movement desensitization and reprocessing (EMDR) therapy

exposures.details: Standard eight-phase protocol; sessions lasted 60-90 minutes; targets were emotionally disturbing memories related to onset or worsening of misophonia.

canonical_statement: Each EMDR session lasted 60-90 minutes, and treatment ended when SUD was zero for all indexed misophonia-related memories.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Each EMDR session lasted 60–90 minutes. Treatment was ended when the Subjective Units of Distress Scale (SUD) score was zero for all indexed misophonia-related memories identified on the time-line.

concept.text: Eye movement desensitization and reprocessing (EMDR) therapy

exposures.details: Standard eight-phase protocol; sessions lasted 60-90 minutes; targets were emotionally disturbing memories related to onset or worsening of misophonia.

canonical_statement: The primary self-reported outcome was AMISOS-R, a 10-item misophonia symptom scale ranging from 0 to 40, with higher scores indicating greater severity.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Misophonia symptoms were measured using the revised Amsterdam Misophonia Scale (AMISOS-R) ... It consists of 10 items with scores ranging from 0 to 40. Higher scores indicate more severe misophonia.

concept.text: AMISOS-R total score

outcome.definition: 10-item revised Amsterdam Misophonia Scale; 0-40, higher scores indicate greater severity

canonical_statement: The co-primary outcome was the observer-rated CGI-I, scored from 1 (very much improved) to 7 (very much worse).

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The co-primary outcome was CGI-Improvement (CGI-I) ... 1 = very much improved ... 7 = very much worse since the initiation of treatment.

concept.text: Clinical Global Impression-Improvement (CGI-I)

outcome.definition: Observer-rated global improvement score from 1 to 7

canonical_statement: Full response required at least 25% AMISOS-R reduction and CGI-I <3; partial response required either criterion.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Full response was defined by 25% reduction (or more) in the AMISOS-R and a CGI-I score <3. Partial response was defined by either a 25% reduction (or more) on the AMISOS-R or a CGI-I score <3.

concept.text: Treatment response

outcome.definition: Full response: >=25% AMISOS-R reduction plus CGI-I <3; partial response: either criterion

canonical_statement: Participants were assessed at baseline and post-treatment; the post-treatment CGI-I was rated by an independent assessor who was experienced in CBT for misophonia.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients were assessed at baseline (T1), and post treatment (T2). At T2 an independent assessor rated all patients in a clinical interview.

canonical_statement: Because this was a pilot study, no formal sample-size calculation was performed.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Since this is a pilot study no formal sample size calculations were performed.

canonical_statement: Primary symptom change was tested with paired two-tailed t-tests; an additional treated-population analysis used last observation carried forward for missing post-treatment values, and results were considered exploratory.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: An additional intention-to-treat analysis was performed, including all patients who received EMDR therapy, irrespective of whether they completed the therapy. Missing values were hereby imputed by the last observation carried forward (LOCF). All analyses were all based on 2-tailed t-tests. ... All results should be considered as exploratory.

canonical_statement: Among seven completers, mean AMISOS-R decreased from 30.43 to 24.29, a mean change of -6.14 points (SD 5.34; p=.023).

canonical_statement: The uncontrolled case-series design cannot separate EMDR effects from time or non-specific factors.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The lack of a control group prevents us from assessing the effects of time and of non-specific factors on misophonia symptoms.

canonical_statement: The small sample warrants caution in generalizing the findings.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The small sample warrants caution in the generalization of the results.

canonical_statement: There was no follow-up assessment because participants on the CBT waiting list received CBT after EMDR, so maintenance of treatment gains could not be determined.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: There was no follow-up assessment since half of the patients were on the waiting list for CBT and received CBT following EMDR, making it impossible to determine whether treatment gain was maintained over time.

canonical_statement: The study included two subpopulations: patients waiting for CBT and prior CBT nonresponders.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The inclusion of two subpopulations can be considered a limitation in this small sample.

canonical_statement: All participants received EMDR from one therapist; the evaluator was not blinded, and treatment-fidelity measures were not performed.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: All participants received EMDR from one therapist, the evaluator was not blind to treatment and treatment fidelity measures were not carried out, possibly leading to bias.

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that EMDR appeared promising and time-limited for reducing misophonia symptoms, including in some prior CBT nonresponders, but emphasized that the findings were preliminary because of the study design.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In conclusion, the results of this study suggest that EMDR therapy is a promising and time-limited intervention in reducing misophonia symptoms ... Given the limitations due to the study design, the results should be considered preliminary.

canonical_statement: The authors recommended replication in a larger randomized trial comparing EMDR with CBT and a waiting list, or testing EMDR as an add-on to CBT, with long-term follow-up.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The next step would therefore be replication of the results in a larger RCT comparing EMDR therapy (with an extended target selection) with CBT and a waiting list or EMDR therapy as an add-on intervention to CBT, with a long-term follow-up.
